comparisons.peer_topic: Net Charge-Offs and Provision for Credit Losses Drivers
comparisons.peer_summary: Net charge-offs for 2024 were $6.0 billion, up from $3.8 billion in 2023, primarily due to credit card loans and the commercial real estate office portfolio. The provision for credit losses increased $1.4 billion to $5.8 billion, driven by credit card and small business loan growth and asset quality deterioration in commercial real estate office and credit card portfolios.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan Chase (JPM) and Bank of America (BAC) disclose the composition of their 2024 provision for credit losses, highlighting that Card Services/Credit Cards were primary drivers of both charge-offs and allowance additions. JPM reported a $10.7 billion provision with $8.6 billion in net charge-offs, noting a $1.2 billion allowance addition predominantly driven by Card Services (as referenced in the prior year comparison context of $6.9B prior year provision). BAC reported a $5.8 billion provision, with net charge-offs of $6.0 billion, also stating that the provision was primarily driven by credit card loan growth and deterioration in credit card portfolios.

sentences.text: The provision in the prior year was $6.9 billion, reflecting net charge-offs of $5.3 billion, a $1.2 billion net addition to the allowance for credit losses, predominantly driven by Card Services, and a $408 million net addition to the allowance for credit losses to establish the allowance for the First Republic loans and lending-related commitments in the second quarter of 2023.
Net charge-offs for 2024 were $6.0 billion compared to $3.8 billion in 2023 primarily due to credit card loans and the commercial real estate office portfolio.

The provision for credit losses in 2024 was primarily driven by credit card as well as small business loan growth, and asset quality deterioration in the commercial real estate office and credit card portfolios.

comparisons.peer_summary: Net credit losses increased 40% to $9.0 billion, with consumer net credit losses rising 39% to $8.6 billion and corporate net credit losses increasing to $397 million from $250 million.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and Citigroup (C) report significant increases in net credit losses/charge-offs in 2024, with consumer credit cards being a major driver for both. JPM's prior year provision comparison highlights the shift in provision drivers, while C explicitly states that net credit losses increased 40% to $9.0 billion, with consumer net credit losses rising 39% to $8.6 billion, largely reflecting continued rise in net credit loss rates in Branded Cards. Both disclosures underscore the severity of consumer credit card credit quality deterioration in 2024 compared to prior periods.
